Representative Publications (selected):.Title: Seed dormancy and germination under winter conditions in Alnus maritima (seaside alder) and the role of canopy disturbance
Representative Publications (selected):.Core Focus: Ecology of regeneration and establishment in a rare riparian tree; seed dormancy/germination dynamics; microbiome interactions; disturbance regimes as recruitment constraints
Representative Publications (selected):.Key Methods/Approach: Seed stratification regimes (NS, 32D, 64D, 96D, 128D, 160D); field burial at 20 cm; two temperature regimes; ANOVA, Tukey’s HSD; Kaplan–Meier; Extended Cox with Hv functions; NLME for leaf chemistry and isotopes; field transplant and microbiome inoculation
Representative Publications (selected):.Main Contributions: Identified non-deep conditional dormancy; demonstrated that root microbiomes can transiently affect seedling establishment and that disturbance regimes can influence survival; advised management strategies emphasizing out-planting older individuals and assessing soil biota interactions

Representative Publications (selected):.Title: BETTSI: A tree-thinking diagnostic tool to assess individual elements of representational competence
Representative Publications (selected):.Core Focus: Development, validation, and reliability testing of BETTSI (Basic Evolutionary Tree-Thinking Skills Instrument) for reading and interpreting phylogenetic trees
Representative Publications (selected):.Key Methods/Approach: Instrument development grounded in seven tree-thinking elements; validity (face, construct) and reliability (KR-20, split-half, test-retest); item analysis; exploratory factor analysis (EFA) using SPSS 25; open educational resource on QUBESHub
Representative Publications (selected):.Main Contributions: Provides a concise, reliable, and open-access diagnostic for tree-thinking proficiency suitable for formative and summative use in introductory biology

Representative Publications (selected):.Title: Bet-hedging against larval herbivory and seed-bank mortality in the evolution of heterocarpy
Representative Publications (selected):.Core Focus: Integration of predispersal herbivory and postdispersal mortality into bet-hedging theory governing heterocarpy in Grindelia ciliata
Representative Publications (selected):.Key Methods/Approach: Two experiments: predispersal mortality with oviposition timing; seed-bank and seedling emergence experiments with stratification/scarification; Bayesian MCMCglmm for predation and survival; Kaplan–Meier; Cox models; life-cycle bet-hedging models
Representative Publications (selected):.Main Contributions: Demonstrated that predispersal mortality can shape optimal seed-type allocation; extended bet-hedging theory to include predispersal mortality and environmental variability; provided empirical and theoretical synthesis

Representative Publications (selected):.Title: Data literacy in life sciences education: frameworks, pathways, and practical guidance
Representative Publications (selected):.Core Focus: Synthesis of Life Discovery Conference discussions; framework for data literacy in biology education; practical steps for embedding data-literacy across curricula
Representative Publications (selected):.Key Methods/Approach: Conceptual framework with four facets of data literacy (collection, calculation, analysis, communication) and a three-level progression; matrix and pathway for developing data skills; emphasis on using existing teaching resources
Representative Publications (selected):.Main Contributions: Articulates a scalable, coordinated approach to teach data literacy in biology, with actionable guidance for instructors and departments

Representative Publications (selected):.Title: Botanical Phylo-Card Game: A hands-on activity integrating tree thinking with phenotypic and gene-pattern data
Representative Publications (selected):.Core Focus: Card-sorting activity to teach plant evolution and tree thinking by combining phenotype-based grouping with rbcL dot-pattern data to illustrate data congruence
Representative Publications (selected):.Key Methods/Approach: Two-phase sorting rounds (phenotype-based, then data-backed with rbcL dot-patterns); visualization of phylogenies; NGSS alignment; large-format and standard card sets
Representative Publications (selected):.Main Contributions: Provides an engaging, scalable classroom/outreach activity that reinforces phylogenetic reasoning and data-congruence concepts for diverse learners

Key Findings & Contributions Across Work: Demonstrated that seed and seedling-stage factors, including microbiomes and disturbance, can be stronger determinants of recruitment than seed survival alone in rare riparian taxa.
Advocated integrating empirical ecology with advanced statistical modeling (survival analysis, Bayesian mixed models) to understand complex life-history traits and recruitment constraints.
Established BETTSI as a validated, openly accessible diagnostic for tree-thinking, addressing a key instructional need in biology education.
Extended bet-hedging theory to include predispersal mortality, highlighting the role of herbivory and seed-bank dynamics in shaping reproductive strategies.
Created practical, scalable educational tools (Phylo-Card Game, data-literacy framework) that bridge theory and classroom practice, with broad applicability from K-12 to undergraduate settings.

Summary Description:: Dr. J. Phil Gibson is an OU-based researcher whose scholarly portfolio spans plant ecology and restoration genetics, seed biology and microbiome interactions, evolutionary bet-hedging theory, and biology education research. His work integrates rigorous field and greenhouse experiments with advanced statistical modeling (including survival analyses and Bayesian mixed models) and theoretical population models to address recruitment constraints in rare plant species and to illuminate factors shaping seed traits. He also contributes to education-focused scholarship by developing tools for tree-thinking assessment (BETTSI) and data-literacy frameworks, and by designing hands-on, scalable educational activities (e.g., Botanical Phylo-Card Game) that align with NGSS. His collaborative network spans multiple OU departments and interdisciplinary partners, reflecting a commitment to bridging ecological science, evolutionary theory, and science education.
